sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听NPR的《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: If you had to choose a romantic partner, would you pick someone who was equally wonderful to everyone,
sentences.zh: 如果你必须选择一个浪漫的伴侣，你会选择一个对所有人（

sentences.en: including you, or someone who was especially wonderful to you?
sentences.zh: 包括你）都同样好的人，还是一个对你特别好的人？

sentences.en: It's a question that fascinates Laleen Anik.
sentences.zh: 这是让拉琳·阿尼克着迷的问题。

sentences.en: I am an assistant professor at University of Virginia's Darden School of Business.
sentences.zh: 我是弗吉尼亚大学达顿商学院的助理教授。

sentences.en: Laleen and her colleague, Ryan Hauser, ran a set of studies to figure out
sentences.zh: 拉琳和她的同事瑞安·豪瑟进行了一系列研究，以弄清楚

sentences.en: if people want a partner who's equal opportunity in their attention
sentences.zh: 人们是想要一个在注意力上机会均等的伴侣，

sentences.en: or someone who reserves special treatment for them.
sentences.zh: 还是想要一个为他们保留特殊对待的人。

sentences.en: What we find in the paper is people want to be treated uniquely.
sentences.zh: 我们在论文中发现的是，人们希望被独特地对待。

sentences.en: The urge to be treated special was so strong that people were willing to pay a price for it.
sentences.zh: 渴望被特殊对待的冲动如此强烈，以至于人们愿意为此付出代价。

sentences.en: Take the example of a birthday message.
sentences.zh: 以生日祝福为例。

sentences.en: Imagine that your partner writes a Facebook message that is long and beautiful.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你的伴侣在脸书上写了一条又长又漂亮的祝福信息。

sentences.en: But there's a catch.
sentences.zh: 但有个问题。

sentences.en: Your partner writes this sort of long birthday message all the time for everyone.
sentences.zh: 你的伴侣对所有人总是写这种长篇生日祝福。

sentences.en: If this message goes to everybody, people say,
sentences.zh: 如果这条信息发给每一个人，人们就会说，

sentences.en: I don't want that beautiful, thoughtful message.
sentences.zh: 我不要那个美丽、体贴的信息。

sentences.en: Just tell me one-liner that says, happy birthday.
sentences.zh: 只要对我说一句“生日快乐”就行了。

sentences.en: Why would people care so much about being singled out that they'd accept an inferior message?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们会如此在乎被特殊对待，以至于愿意接受一条较差的信息？

sentences.en: If my partner sends me a beautiful message,
sentences.zh: 如果我的伴侣发给我一条美丽的信息，

sentences.en: that's a world in which he or he gives it to everybody else.
sentences.zh: 那是一个他也把这发给所有其他人的世界。

sentences.en: And that pie might be bigger, but it is divided into multiple parts.
sentences.zh: 而那块蛋糕可能更大，但它被分成了多份。

sentences.en: And I think people have the feeling that they're getting less.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们有一种感觉，即他们得到的变少了。

sentences.en: In the other world, where they send me a short, almost curt or cold message,
sentences.zh: 在另一个世界里，他们发给我一条简短、几乎生硬或冷淡的信息，

sentences.en: but they don't do that for everybody else,
sentences.zh: 但他们对其他人并非如此，

sentences.en: that means that the whole pie, although it might be smaller, it is mine.
sentences.zh: 这意味着整个蛋糕虽然可能更小，但它是我的。

sentences.en: But it is all for me.
sentences.zh: 而且它完全是属于我的。

sentences.en: So many of us want our partners to give us the whole pie.
sentences.zh: 我们当中有很多人希望我们的伴侣把整个蛋糕给我们。

sentences.en: We expect our loved ones to make us the center of their lives,
sentences.zh: 我们期望所爱的人让我们成为他们生活的中心，

sentences.en: and we expect to do the same in return.
sentences.zh: 我们也期望回报以同样的方式。

sentences.en: Showering favors on those we love doesn't just feel natural.
sentences.zh: 对我们爱的人倾注恩惠不仅感觉很自然。

sentences.en: It feels like something to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是一件值得庆祝的事。

sentences.en: Our Facebook and Instagram feeds are chock full of people describing how they've put their loved ones on a pedestal.
sentences.zh: 我们的脸书和照片墙动态里充满了人们描述他们如何将所爱之人奉为至宝。

sentences.en: But what we fail to notice is that our impulse to give special treatment to those closest to us
sentences.zh: 但我们没有注意到的是，我们将特殊对待给予身边最亲近之人的冲动

sentences.en: can have terrible moral consequences.
sentences.zh: 会带来可怕的道德后果。

sentences.en: Last week, we looked at how few of us actually live by the maxim that everyone is equal.
sentences.zh: 上周，我们探讨了我们当中实际按照“人人平等”这一准则生活的人是多么少。

sentences.en: Today, we try to understand why we struggle to put that value into practice,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们试图理解为什么我们难以将这一价值观付诸实践，

sentences.en: and how actions that come from a place of love can lead to a more unjust world.
sentences.zh: 以及源于爱的行为如何导致一个更加不公正的世界。

sentences.en: The Sins of Playing Favorites, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 偏心的罪过，本周《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Mazarin Banaji has been studying the psychology of discrimination for a long time.
sentences.zh: 马扎林·巴纳吉长期以来一直在研究歧视心理学。

sentences.en: Her first article on the topic came out in 1993,
sentences.zh: 她关于这个主题的第一篇文章发表于1993年，

sentences.en: and she's published hundreds of research papers since then.
sentences.zh: 从那以后她发表了数百篇研究论文。

sentences.en: She's also helped to develop the Implicit Association Test,
sentences.zh: 她还协助开发了隐式联想测验，

sentences.en: which millions of people have used to identify their unconscious biases.
sentences.zh: 数百万人用它来识别他们的无意识偏见。

sentences.en: Given how deeply she's thought about the ways we treat others,
sentences.zh: 鉴于她对我们对待他人方式的深刻思考，

sentences.en: you might think it would take a lot to alter her views about discrimination.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为需要付出很大努力才能改变她对歧视的看法。

sentences.en: But Mazarin's understanding of how bias plays out was radically reshaped by two words.
sentences.zh: 但马扎林对偏见如何发挥作用的理解被两个词彻底重塑了。

sentences.en: Professor Kaplan.
sentences.zh: 卡普兰教授。

sentences.en: Those words marked a turning point in a story she first heard many years ago.
sentences.zh: 这些词标志着她多年前听过的一个故事的转折点。

sentences.en: The story was about Mazarin's friend and colleague, Carla Kaplan.
sentences.zh: 这个故事关于马扎林的朋友兼同事卡拉·卡普兰。

sentences.en: Carla and Mazarin are now both professors in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 卡拉和马扎林现在都是马萨诸塞州的教授。

sentences.en: Carla at Northeastern University and Mazarin at Harvard.
sentences.zh: 卡拉在东北大学，马扎林在哈佛。

sentences.en: But at the time, they both taught at Yale.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，他们都在耶鲁教书。

sentences.en: Carla was this absolutely brilliant young woman,
sentences.zh: 卡拉曾经是一个绝对聪明的年轻女性，

sentences.en: articulate beyond measure, gifted writer, a professor of English.
sentences.zh: 言辞无可挑剔，才华横溢的作家，英语教授。

sentences.en: But she also had these wonderful other hobbies.
sentences.zh: 但她也有这些极好的其他爱好。

sentences.en: I mean, she was a quilter, and you would often see her sitting in the back of a lecture,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她是个拼布工，你经常会看到她坐在讲座后面，

sentences.en: like a little Madame Defarge, you know, sitting there quilting away
sentences.zh: 就像一个小德法奇夫人，你知道，坐在那里一边缝拼布，

sentences.en: while she listened to a talk on 18th century, you know, literature.
sentences.zh: 一边听关于18世纪文学的讲座。

sentences.en: Despite working in different departments,
sentences.zh: 尽管在不同的系工作，

sentences.en: the two of them got to know each other
sentences.zh: 他们两个还是互相认识了，

sentences.en: because they shared a characteristic that was unusual for professors in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 因为他们有着一项在20世纪80年代的教授中并不常见的特征。

sentences.en: They were women.
sentences.zh: 他们是女性。

sentences.en: In the late 1980s, young women, women who looked like us,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪80年代末，年轻女性，长得像我们这样的女性，

sentences.en: could only be two kinds of people.
sentences.zh: 只能是两种人。

sentences.en: If they dressed like us, they looked like undergraduates.
sentences.zh: 如果她们的穿着像我们，她们看起来就像本科生。

sentences.en: And if they dressed nicer, they typically were administrative assistants.
sentences.zh: 如果她们穿得更好一点，她们通常是行政助理。

sentences.en: The few female professors on campus regularly crossed paths.
sentences.zh: 校园里为数不多的女教授经常有交集。

sentences.en: That's what happened to Mazarin and Carla.
sentences.zh: 马扎林和卡拉就是这样认识的。

sentences.en: And we got to know each other,
sentences.zh: 我们互相认识了，

sentences.en: which is how I learned about the story of her hand.
sentences.zh: 这就是我如何得知她手的故事的。

sentences.en: One night, Carla lost her grip on a crystal bowl she was washing.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，卡拉在洗一个水晶碗时没拿稳。

sentences.en: The bowl hit the sink and shattered.
sentences.zh: 碗撞到水槽上碎了。

sentences.en: The jagged edge of this bowl cut her hand from the middle of the palm to her wriSt.
sentences.zh: 这个碗锋利的边缘从她手掌中间一直割到了手腕。

sentences.en: Carla's kitchen floor looked like a Jackson Pollock canvas.
sentences.zh: 卡拉的厨房地板看起来像杰克逊·波洛克的画布。

sentences.en: Her blood was splattered everywhere.
sentences.zh: 她的血溅得到处都是。

sentences.en: Her boyfriend patched up her hand with some bandages.
sentences.zh: 她的男友用一些绷带简单处理了她的手。

sentences.en: He rushed her over to the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 他把她紧急送到急诊室。

sentences.en: The attending doctor was very attentive to her and kept reassuring her that she would be fine.
sentences.zh: 主治医生对她非常周到，并一直安慰她会没事的。

sentences.en: Carla and her boyfriend tried to get the doctor to understand how important it was for Carla to preserve the dexterity in her hand.
sentences.zh: 卡拉和她的男友试图让医生明白保持手部灵活性对卡拉有多么重要。

sentences.en: They explained that she was a quilter.
sentences.zh: 他们解释说她是一名拼布工。

sentences.en: Quilting requires fine finger movement.
sentences.zh: 拼布需要手指做精细运动。

sentences.en: And they hoped that this stitching up would actually allow her to have all of her sensitivity back in her hands.
sentences.zh: 他们希望这次缝合实际上能让她的手恢复所有的知觉。

sentences.en: And were assured that indeed that would happen.
sentences.zh: 并且他们得到保证，事实确实会如此。

sentences.en: And there was no reason to think in that moment that she wasn't receiving anything but the best treatment.
sentences.zh: 当时没有任何理由认为她受到的不是最好的治疗。

sentences.en: But Carla was about to discover that she was not getting the best treatment possible.
sentences.zh: 但卡拉即将发现她并没有得到最好的可能治疗。

sentences.en: A volunteer at the hospital happened to pass by, recognized Carla, and said,
sentences.zh: 医院的一位志愿者恰巧路过，认出了卡拉，并说：

sentences.en: Professor Kaplan, what are you doing here?
sentences.zh: 卡普兰教授，你在这里做什么？

sentences.en: The doctor froze.
sentences.zh: 医生僵住了。

sentences.en: He asked Carla,
sentences.zh: 他问卡拉：

sentences.en: You're a professor at Yale?
sentences.zh: 你是耶鲁的教授？

sentences.en: Upon confirming that information, rushed Carla off to a different part of the building.
sentences.zh: 在确认了这一信息后，医生急忙把卡拉送到了大楼的另一个区域。

sentences.en: The best hand specialist in New England was called.
sentences.zh: 新英格兰最好的手部专家被请来了。

sentences.en: And with a bunch of other doctors, operated on her hand for several hours into the night.
sentences.zh: 在一群其他医生的配合下，为她的手进行了几个小时直到深夜的手术。

sentences.en: It was far more extensive surgery than Carla would have received in the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 这比卡拉在急诊室接受的手术要广泛得多。

sentences.en: The work on the finer nerves of her hand is what would have taken the incredibly longer time.
sentences.zh: 对她手部更细微神经的处理耗费了极其长的时间。

sentences.en: And then I also believe that there was greater attention to the cosmetic part of it.
sentences.zh: 而且我还相信，医生对外观美容部分给予了更多的关注。

sentences.en: Carla was grateful to receive such careful attention.
sentences.zh: 卡拉很感激能得到如此周到的照顾。

sentences.en: But her gratitude was overshadowed by another feeling.
sentences.zh: 但她的感激被另一种感觉所掩盖。

sentences.en: She was appalled.
sentences.zh: 她感到震惊。

sentences.en: Carla was just stunned that her being a quilter was not sufficient to get her the treatment
sentences.zh: 卡拉简直惊呆了，她是一名拼布工并不足以让她得到她

sentences.en: that she should have gotten, but that being a professor did.
sentences.zh: 本该得到的治疗，而身为教授却可以。

sentences.en: And somehow, it must be that the doctor did not feel compelled by the quilter story
sentences.zh: 不知何故，医生一定是没有被拼布工的故事所打动，

sentences.en: in the same way as he was compelled by a two-word phrase, Yale professor.
sentences.zh: 就像他被一个双词短语“耶鲁教授”所打动一样。

sentences.en: When Mazarin reflected on the story, it rattled her understanding of bias, the very focus of
sentences.zh: 当马扎林反思这个故事时，它动摇了她对偏见的理解——而偏见正是她

sentences.en: her career.
sentences.zh: 职业生涯的焦点。

sentences.en: Had Carla's doctor in the ER refused to perform surgery on her because of her race or gender
sentences.zh: 如果急诊室的医生因为卡拉的种族、性别

sentences.en: or some other characteristic, Mazarin would have immediately considered what happened to
sentences.zh: 或其他特征而拒绝为她做手术，马扎林会立即认为发生的事情

sentences.en: be discrimination.
sentences.zh: 是歧视。

sentences.en: We all would.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都会。

sentences.en: But Carla was not denied anything.
sentences.zh: 但卡拉并没有被剥夺任何东西。

sentences.en: The emergency room doctor was kind, attentive, and competent.
sentences.zh: 急诊室医生很善良、体贴且称职。

sentences.en: Carla was not treated worse than any other patient.
sentences.zh: 卡拉受到的待遇并不比任何其他患者差。

sentences.en: The point of the Carla story is to focus not so much on a negative thing that the doctor
sentences.zh: 卡拉的故事的重点与其说是关注医生所做的消极事情，

sentences.en: did, something where he withheld some basic level attention to her.
sentences.zh: 即他扣留了对她的某种基本程度的关怀。

sentences.en: What we're speaking about here are acts of helping, which are things that go above and beyond what
sentences.zh: 我们在这里谈论的是施以援手的行为，这些行为超出了

sentences.en: we typically do.
sentences.zh: 我们通常所做的范畴。

sentences.en: The moral problem at the heart of Carla's story was not an act of hate, but an act of
sentences.zh: 卡拉故事核心的道德问题不是出于仇恨的行为，而是出于

sentences.en: special kindness.
sentences.zh: 特殊善意的行为。

sentences.en: What Carla got went above and beyond the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 卡拉得到的超越了寻常。

sentences.en: She received VIP treatment, and it made a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 她受到了VIP级别的待遇，这产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: It's hard for me to think that a patch-up job in an ER that required sewing up versus fine-grained
sentences.zh: 我很难想象，急诊室里需要缝合的简单处理与持续数小时的精细

sentences.en: surgery that goes on for hours is really not going to have some substantial impact on the
sentences.zh: 手术相比，真的不会对这个人的生活产生

sentences.en: person's life.
sentences.zh: 重大影响吗？

sentences.en: Mazarin realized that our definition of discrimination is too narrow to capture this type of harm.
sentences.zh: 马扎林意识到，我们对歧视的定义太狭隘了，无法捕捉这种类型的伤害。

sentences.en: We really measure prejudice in the old-fashioned way by looking for acts of commission.
sentences.zh: 我们确实是通过寻找作为的行为，以老式的方式来衡量偏见。

sentences.en: What do I do?
sentences.zh: 我做了什么？

sentences.en: Do I go across a town to burn down the church of somebody who's not from my denomination?
sentences.zh: 我会横穿小镇去烧毁一个不属于我教派的人的教堂吗？

sentences.en: That I can recognize as prejudice.
sentences.zh: 我能认出那是偏见。

sentences.en: But when we don't act, that's acceptable.
sentences.zh: 但当我们不作为时，那是可以接受的。

sentences.en: It's understandable that we rarely feel outraged when someone gets treated better.
sentences.zh: 当有人受到更好的对待时，我们很少感到愤怒，这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: We don't see the harm because the harm is invisible.
sentences.zh: 我们看不到伤害，因为伤害是无形的。

sentences.en: It's directed at people who don't get the VIP treatment.
sentences.zh: 它是针对那些没有得到VIP待遇的人的。

sentences.en: But those people were not in the ER with Carla.
sentences.zh: 但这些人当时没有和卡拉在急诊室里。

sentences.en: They didn't know what they were missing.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道自己错过了什么。

sentences.en: If you haven't benefited from this type of treatment, you might have suspicions that favoritism
sentences.zh: 如果你没有从这种待遇中受益，你可能会怀疑偏袒

sentences.en: is costing you opportunities, but it's often hard to pinpoint what you're losing.
sentences.zh: 让你失去了机会，但通常很难准确指出你正在失去什么。

sentences.en: You don't know what would have happened if someone had recommended you for a job because
sentences.zh: 你不知道如果有人因为你们俩上了同一所大学

sentences.en: you both went to the same university.
sentences.zh: 而把你推荐给某个工作，会发生什么。

sentences.en: Or how your career would have changed if you had been invited to a private party where important
sentences.zh: 或者如果你被邀请参加讨论重要公司业务的私人聚会，

sentences.en: company business got discussed.
sentences.zh: 你的职业生涯会如何改变。

sentences.en: For Mazarin, the experience that Carla described in the hospital was like a curtain being pulled
sentences.zh: 对于马扎林来说，卡拉在医院描述的经历就像是拉开了一道

sentences.en: back.
sentences.zh: 帷幕。

sentences.en: Carla suddenly got to see what it was like to be treated the same as everyone else and what
sentences.zh: 卡拉突然得以看到像其他人一样被对待是什么感觉，

sentences.en: it was like to be treated as someone special.
sentences.zh: 以及被当作特殊人物对待是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Carla Kaplan and Professor Kaplan each got a glimpse of what life was like for the other person.
sentences.zh: 卡拉·卡普兰和卡普兰教授各自得以一窥对方的生活是什么样的。

sentences.en: It made Mazarin reflect on her own behavior.
sentences.zh: 这促使马扎林反思她自己的行为。

sentences.en: I go through life having no clue that the people around me are the ones I'm helping unless
sentences.zh: 我在生活中度过，完全不知道周围的人正是我在给予帮助的人，除非

sentences.en: I pause and ask the question, how do I wish to do this?
sentences.zh: 我停下来问自己：我希望如何做到这一点？

sentences.en: Do I intend to help one type of person over another?
sentences.zh: 我打算帮助某一类人而不帮助另一类人吗？

sentences.en: Mazarin can think of instances when she's favored people because they shared something in common
sentences.zh: 马扎林能想到一些她曾偏袒某些人的例子，因为这些人与她有

sentences.en: with her.
sentences.zh: 某些共同点。

sentences.en: Like the time a writer asked to interview her for a story.
sentences.zh: 就像有一次，一位作家要求采访她，写一篇报道。

sentences.en: I typically oblige but I asked her who she was writing for and when she told me I said
sentences.zh: 我通常都会答应，但我问她是在为谁写稿，当她告诉我之后，我说

sentences.en: I don't think I'll do the interview because I did not hold the magazine she was writing

sentences.en: And then the next level up is based on a kind of reciprocity in a direct face-to-face sort
sentences.zh: 而下一个层级的合作则基于某种直接面对面的

sentences.en: of way.
sentences.zh: 互惠方式。

sentences.en: So, this is, you know, friends.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是朋友。

sentences.en: You'd share food with each other, you'd have each other's backs when going into battle,
sentences.zh: 你们会彼此分享食物，上战场时会守望相助，

sentences.en: take care of each other's children, take care of each other when you're sick.
sentences.zh: 照顾彼此的孩子，在对方生病时互相照料。

sentences.en: That's what friends are for, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是朋友存在的意义，对吧？

sentences.en: And everybody is likely to do better if they have other people that they can cooperate with.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都有可以合作的其他伙伴，他们的处境都可能会更好。

sentences.en: You can imagine the circle of cooperation expanding even further.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，合作的圈子还在进一步扩大。

sentences.en: You get out to different levels where there might be people who you don't know personally,
sentences.zh: 你会进入不同的层面，在那里可能会有一些你并不面熟的人，

sentences.en: but you have some kind of connection with.
sentences.zh: 但你与他们某种程度上有着联系。

sentences.en: That is, you're a member of the same religion, or you're a member of the same country,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你们信仰相同的宗教，或者属于同一个国家，

sentences.en: or you have some other kinds of shared connections or interests, or you're a friend of my friend,
sentences.zh: 或者你们有一些其他的共同联系或利益，或者你是我的朋友，

sentences.en: or a friend of a friend of my friend, right?
sentences.zh: 又或者是我的朋友的朋友，对吧？

sentences.en: Then, you know, those are more symbolically marked.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，这些会带有更多象征性的标志。

sentences.en: It's not based on your experience with that person, but what you have encoded about them
sentences.zh: 它不是基于你与那个人的实际交往经验，而是基于你对他们的理解，

sentences.en: in a more abstract kind of way.
sentences.zh: 一种更抽象的编码方式。

sentences.en: There's a simple image you can use to picture this.
sentences.zh: 你可以用一个简单的意象来描绘这一点。

sentences.en: As the philosopher Peter Singer put it, we live in these moral concentric circles.
sentences.zh: 正如哲学家彼得·辛格所说，我们生活在这些道德同心圆中。

sentences.en: If you're a complete narcissist, it's just you at the middle, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你是个彻头彻尾的自恋狂，中心就只有你自己，对吧？

sentences.en: And then one ring out is your family and your closest friends,
sentences.zh: 再往外一层是你的家人和最亲密的朋友，

sentences.en: and then people who you're more acquainted with,
sentences.zh: 然后是与你更熟悉的人，

sentences.en: people who are in a, you know, perhaps part of your town, your village,
sentences.zh: 那些可能生活在你的小镇、你的村庄里的人，

sentences.en: and then broader connections with people,
sentences.zh: 接着是与人们更广泛的联系，

sentences.en: even people who are strangers but are connected to you in some way.
sentences.zh: 甚至是那些与你素不相识、但在某种程度上与你有关联的人。

sentences.en: And so in some sense, the most basic question that anyone has to answer is,
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，每个人都必须回答的最基本问题是：

sentences.en: how big is my us?
sentences.zh: 我们的范围有多大？

sentences.en: What is the range of humans or beings even that I care about?
sentences.zh: 我所关心的人类或甚至生命的范围是什么？

sentences.en: Dylan's circle of care is very large.
sentences.zh: 迪伦的关怀圈非常大。

sentences.en: It's basically the entire world.
sentences.zh: 基本上包含了整个世界。

sentences.en: Hannah's circle is much smaller.
sentences.zh: 汉娜的关怀圈要小得多。

sentences.en: It's her family, her community, her city.
sentences.zh: 它只限于她的家人、她的社区、她的城市。

sentences.en: Few of us operate solely with either of these frameworks.
sentences.zh: 我们很少有人完全只用这两种框架中的某一种来行事。

sentences.en: We move back and forth.
sentences.zh: 我们在它们之间来回切换。

sentences.en: Joshua compares these different moral frameworks to settings on a camera.
sentences.zh: 约书亚将这些不同的道德框架比作相机的设置。

sentences.en: Think about photography,
sentences.zh: 想想摄影，

sentences.en: especially if you're kind of a weak amateur photographer like me.
sentences.zh: 尤其是如果你像我一样，是个半斤八两的业余摄影爱好者。

sentences.en: So the camera that I've used for years has these nice automatic settings.
sentences.zh: 我用了好几年的相机有这些很棒的自动设置。

sentences.en: So if I want to take a picture of a mountain from a mile away,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我想在一英里外拍摄一张高山的照片，

sentences.en: then I put it in landscape setting and click, point, and shoot,
sentences.zh: 我就会把它调到风景模式，然后对准、按下快门，

sentences.en: and I've got a pretty good picture of a mountain from far away.
sentences.zh: 就能拍出一张相当不错的远景山脉照片。

sentences.en: Or it has portrait mode and dark mode, et cetera, right?
sentences.zh: 或者它有肖像模式和夜景模式等等，对吧？

sentences.en: And the idea is that the manufacturer has thought in advance,
sentences.zh: 这里的理念是，制造商已经提前考虑过了，

sentences.en: you know, what are the kinds of things that people need to do all the time?
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们经常需要做的事情有哪些？

sentences.en: We're just going to set up these pre-programmed responses for those things.
sentences.zh: 我们只要针对这些事情预设好响应模式就行了。

sentences.en: And that's what people use most of the time.
sentences.zh: 这也是人们绝大多数时间都在使用的功能。

sentences.en: And that's what I do.
sentences.zh: 我也是这么做的。

sentences.en: Occasionally, I get ambitious and will want to do something fancy
sentences.zh: 偶尔我会心血来潮，想搞点花样，

sentences.en: and maybe have something slightly out of focus and off to the side.
sentences.zh: 比如拍出主体微微失焦且偏在一侧的照片。

sentences.en: And who knows, right?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢，对吧？

sentences.en: And so there you put the camera in manual mode.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，你会把相机调到手动模式。

sentences.en: And that allows you to adjust the f-stop and everything else by hand.
sentences.zh: 这能让你手动调整光圈和其他所有参数。

sentences.en: There are benefits to having both of these camera modes.
sentences.zh: 拥有这两种相机模式各有利弊。

sentences.en: It allows you to navigate the trade-off between efficiency and flexibility
sentences.zh: 它能让你在效率与灵活性之间，

sentences.en: or reliability and flexibility.
sentences.zh: 或者说在可靠性与灵活性之间做出权衡。

sentences.en: That is, if I tried to do all those different things that I might do for portraits and landscapes,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果我试图用手动方式完成那些可能用于拍摄人像和风景的各种操作，

sentences.en: by hand I might make a mistake and I'm trying to do this quickly.
sentences.zh: 由于我想快速完成，很可能会出错。

sentences.en: It's much better to have a point-and-shoot setting.
sentences.zh: 有个傻瓜相机式的设置要好得多。

sentences.en: But you can't do everything you might want to do with point-and-shoot settings.
sentences.zh: 但你无法通过傻瓜相机设置完成所有你想做的事。

sentences.en: And that's why the manual mode is great.
sentences.zh: 这就是手动模式大显身手的地方。

sentences.en: And in the same way, we humans have gut reactions.
sentences.zh: 同样地，我们人类也有本能反应。

sentences.en: We have feelings.
sentences.zh: 我们有情感。

sentences.en: We have habits.
sentences.zh: 我们有习惯。

sentences.en: In a familiar kind of situation, you don't even have to think or reason about it
sentences.zh: 在熟悉的情境下，当遇到显然是极其错误的事情时，

sentences.en: when it's something that's just obviously a terrible thing to do.
sentences.zh: 你甚至都不需要去思考或推理。

sentences.en: And that's good.
sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.en: You want to have that kind of efficiency and sturdiness in your everyday basic moral judgment.
sentences.zh: 你希望在日常的基本道德判断中拥有这种效率和稳健性。

sentences.en: But then sometimes life is complicated and sometimes there are difficult trade-offs.
sentences.zh: 但有时生活很复杂，有时也会面临艰难的权衡。

sentences.en: And then that's when you want to shift into manual mode.
sentences.zh: 而那正是你想切换到手动模式的时候。

sentences.en: Joshua finds this analogy helpful because it answers a question that people tend to ask.
sentences.zh: 约书亚发现这个类比很有帮助，因为它回答了人们经常提出的一个问题。

sentences.en: Which moral framework is better?
sentences.zh: 哪种道德框架更好？

sentences.en: And the answer is neither is better.
sentences.zh: 答案是，没有哪个更好。

sentences.en: It depends on what you're trying to do.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你想做什么。

sentences.en: If you're trying to do something quickly, fast, and fairly routine,
sentences.zh: 如果你想快速、敏捷且按常规办事，

sentences.en: then you want the automatic settings.
sentences.zh: 那么你就需要自动设置。

sentences.en: And if you're trying to do something more complicated
sentences.zh: 而如果你想做一些更复杂的事情，

sentences.en: and you're kind of out of your usual element or trying to do something new,
sentences.zh: 并且你有点脱离了平时的舒适区，或者在尝试新事物，

sentences.en: then you want the manual mode.
sentences.zh: 那么你就需要手动模式。

sentences.en: And I think it's the same thing with moral thinking,
sentences.zh: 我想道德思考也是如此，

sentences.en: that when it comes to the ethics of everyday life,
sentences.zh: 当涉及日常生活伦理时，

sentences.en: the basic things that everybody should know not to do,
sentences.zh: 也就是每个人都知道不该去做的那些基本事情，

sentences.en: the lying, stealing, cheating kinds of things,
sentences.zh: 比如撒谎、偷窃、作弊之类的事情，

sentences.en: we want to have automatic settings that just say,
sentences.zh: 我们希望有自动设置，它们会直接说：

sentences.en: nope, nope, nope, nope, nope, nope, can't do that.
sentences.zh: 不行，不行，不行，不行，不行，不能那样做。

sentences.en: But then when we're making difficult decisions,
sentences.zh: 但当我们做出艰难的决定时，

sentences.en: decisions where on the one hand something might feel wrong or break some kind of rule,
sentences.zh: 也就是一方面某种做法可能感觉不对或违反了某种规则，

sentences.en: but on the other hand it could mean more people will die
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，如果你不做那件平时看起来正确的事，

sentences.en: if you do the thing that seems like the ordinarily right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 可能会导致更多人死亡。

sentences.en: Then you want to be able to weigh those things against each other.
sentences.zh: 那么你就需要去权衡这些事情。

sentences.en: And that is exactly what our brains do.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们的大脑所做的事情。

sentences.en: Joshua and other researchers have found that different parts of the brain are at work
sentences.zh: 约书亚和其他研究人员发现，当我们使用手动模式和自动模式时，

sentences.en: when we're using our manual mode and our automatic mode.
sentences.zh: 大脑的不同部分正在工作。

sentences.en: When people are specifically engaging the utilitarian reasoning,
sentences.zh: 当人们专门进行功利主义推理时，

sentences.en: you see increased activity in a part of the brain called the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
sentences.zh: 你会看到大脑中一个被称为背外侧前额叶皮层的区域活动增加。

sentences.en: It's part of a network in our brain that's the home of hard thinking and self-control.
sentences.zh: 它是我们大脑中负责深度思考和自我控制的网络的一部分。

sentences.en: Like if you're trying to remember a long string of numbers or something like that,
sentences.zh: 比如当你试图记住一长串数字或类似事情时，

sentences.en: or if you're resisting an impulse.
sentences.zh: 或者当你在克制某种冲动时。

sentences.en: The automatic mode engages a different part of the brain.
sentences.zh: 自动模式则会激活大脑的不同部位。

sentences.en: The amygdala, which is a kind of early warning attention directing system that says
sentences.zh: 杏仁核，它是一种早期预警和注意力导向系统，会提示说

sentences.en: something's going on here, maybe bad, you've got to pay attention to this.
sentences.zh: 这里有点不对劲，可能很糟糕，你必须注意这一点。

sentences.en: And so if you see a snake, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你看到一条蛇，

sentences.en: before you even realize what you've seen at a sort of conceptual level,
sentences.zh: 甚至在你从概念层面上意识到自己看到了什么之前，

sentences.en: your brain is already responding with that flash of,
sentences.zh: 你的大脑就已经开始做出反应，闪过这样的念头：

sentences.en: whoa, something you need to pay attention to there.
sentences.zh: 哇，那是有必要注意的东西。

sentences.en: Joshua has used dilemmas like the trolley problem
sentences.zh: 约书亚曾用诸如电车难题之类的困境

sentences.en: to understand what happens when we shift between the two modes.
sentences.zh: 来理解我们在两种模式之间切换时会发生什么。

sentences.en: The most revealing scenarios pit the two modes against one another.
sentences.zh: 最具启示意义的场景是将这两种模式置于对立面。

sentences.en: One of these scenarios, the dilemma of the crying baby.
sentences.zh: 其中一个场景就是婴儿啼哭的困境。

sentences.en: This is kind of a horrible case.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当可怕的案例。

sentences.en: And I think when I first started thinking about this,
sentences.zh: 我想我刚开始思考这个问题时，

sentences.en: it was before I had kids.
sentences.zh: 是在我还没当父母之前。

sentences.en: And now that I have kids, it's like even more horrible to think about.
sentences.zh: 而现在我有了孩子，再回想起来就觉得更加可怕了。

sentences.en: But this is modeled after some stories that people told
sentences.zh: 但这模拟了一些人们讲述的

sentences.en: about what happened in World War II.
sentences.zh: 二战期间发生的故事。

sentences.en: And the other story is that people are hiding in a basement
sentences.zh: 另一个故事是，人们躲在地下室里，

sentences.en: and the enemy soldiers are outside and there's a baby that starts to cry.
sentences.zh: 敌方士兵就在外面，这时有个婴儿开始哭闹。

sentences.en: And if the soldiers hear the baby, they'll find everybody
sentences.zh: 如果士兵听到婴儿的哭声，就会找到所有人，

sentences.en: and they'll kill everybody, including the baby.
sentences.zh: 并且会杀死所有人，包括那个婴儿。

sentences.en: Is it morally acceptable to smother the baby in order to save everybody else,
sentences.zh: 为了拯救其他人而闷死婴儿，在道德上是否可以接受？

sentences.en: knowing that the baby would die anyway if you didn't do anything?
sentences.zh: 明知如果你什么都不做，婴儿无论如何也会死。

sentences.en: Compared to the standard version of the trolley problem,
sentences.zh: 与标准版的电车难题相比，

sentences.en: the crying baby case ramps up the stakes.
sentences.zh: 婴儿啼哭的案例提高了赌注。

sentences.en: One, it's your own child as opposed to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 第一，那是你自己的孩子，而不是陌生人。

sentences.en: And at least the way the story is described,
sentences.zh: 至少按照故事的描述，

sentences.en: the child's going to die anyway if you don't do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你不那样做，孩子无论如何都会死。

sentences.en: And so that's something that also seems to matter.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一个似乎很关键的因素。

sentences.en: That is, in general, people are more willing to say that it's okay
sentences.zh: 也就是说，总的来说，如果这件可怕的事情涉及伤害某个

sentences.en: to do the horrible thing in the name of the greater good
sentences.zh: 无论如何最终都会受到伤害的人，

sentences.en: if the horrible thing involves hurting somebody
sentences.zh: 人们更愿意承认为了更大的利益

sentences.en: who would end up being harmed anyway.
sentences.zh: 去做这件可怕的事情是可以接受的。

sentences.en: If you give people brain scans as they consider such dilemmas,
sentences.zh: 如果你在人们思考此类困境时对他们进行脑部扫描，

sentences.en: you can almost see different parts of their minds wrestle with something
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以看到他们大脑的不同部分在进行一番挣扎：

sentences.en: that feels viscerally wrong but logically correct.
sentences.zh: 一边是直觉上觉得不对，另一边则是逻辑上正确。

sentences.en: When people have to make an all-things-considered judgment,
sentences.zh: 当人们必须做出综合考量的判断时，

sentences.en: where they are not told to just think about your feelings
sentences.zh: 这时没有人要求你只去考虑自己的感受，

sentences.en: or just think about the consequences,
sentences.zh: 或者只去考虑后果，

sentences.en: but instead try to weigh those things against each other,
sentences.zh: 而是试着去权衡这些不同的因素，

sentences.en: you see increased activity in a part of the brain
sentences.zh: 你会发现大脑某个区域的活动有所增加

sentences.en: called the ventromedial prefrontal cortex.
sentences.zh: 被称为腹内侧前额叶皮层。

sentences.en: This part of the brain integrates these two different types of decision-making.
sentences.zh: 大脑的这部分整合了这两种不同类型的决策。

sentences.en: It's like these different weights get added up
sentences.zh: 就像这些不同的权重被累加起来

sentences.en: and the scale tips one way or another,
sentences.zh: 天平倾向于这一边或那一边，

sentences.en: and that's how we decide what to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们决定要做什么的方式。

sentences.en: We told you a second ago that one system for moral reasoning
sentences.zh: 我们刚才告诉过你，道德推理的一个系统

sentences.en: is not better than the other.
sentences.zh: 并不比另一个更好。

sentences.en: That's true, but not always.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但并非总是如此。

sentences.en: There are situations in our modern world
sentences.zh: 在我们的现代世界中，有些情况下

sentences.en: for which the fast, intuitive system in our heads
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中那个快速、直觉的系统

sentences.en: is not well-designed.
sentences.zh: 设计得并不好。

sentences.en: This system was not designed for a world
sentences.zh: 这个系统并非为了这样一个世界而设计

sentences.en: in which we no longer live in tribes,
sentences.zh: 在这个世界里，我们不再生活在部落中，

sentences.en: where the people who live near us don't always look like us.
sentences.zh: 住在我们附近的人并不总是长得和我们一样。

sentences.en: They were not designed for a time
sentences.zh: 它们不是为了那个时代而设计的

sentences.en: when we're capable of helping people on the other side of the world.
sentences.zh: 那时我们有能力帮助世界另一端的人。

sentences.en: When Dylan thinks about the balance between these modes of moral reasoning,
sentences.zh: 当迪伦思考这几种道德推理模式之间的平衡时，

sentences.en: his mind jumps to cases where loyalty and love cause real harm.
sentences.zh: 他的脑海里浮现出忠诚和爱造成真正伤害的案例。

sentences.en: One example, he says, are the ways in which some men have responded to concerns
sentences.zh: 他说，其中一个例子是某些男性对关切的回应方式

sentences.en: about sexual misconduct.
sentences.zh: 关于性行为不端。

sentences.en: There have been a lot of stories of the nature of,
sentences.zh: 有很多这样性质的故事，

sentences.en: hey, I'm a guy in media or politics or entertainment.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是个搞媒体、政治或娱乐的家伙。

sentences.en: I've heard rumors about this guy friend of mine
sentences.zh: 我过去几年听到过关于我这位男性朋友的传闻

sentences.en: being awful toward women for the last few years.
sentences.zh: 他对女性态度恶劣。

sentences.en: I'm not going to say anything because I feel like he's a good guy
sentences.zh: 我什么都不说，因为我觉得他是个好人

sentences.en: and he deserves better than for me to stick my neck out
sentences.zh: 他值得我不要挺身而出

sentences.en: and get into his business.
sentences.zh: 去插手他的事。

sentences.en: That's about a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 这涉及到很多事情。

sentences.en: That's about endemic misogyny and depression and accountability.
sentences.zh: 这关乎根深蒂固的厌女症、消沉和问责制。

sentences.en: But I think it's also about men placing loyalty before other virtues.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这也关乎男性将忠诚置于其他美德之上。

sentences.en: And in a family context, I've had some experience of people
sentences.zh: 在家庭语境下，我有一些这样的经历

sentences.en: acting like the fact that we are family and loyal to each other
